extracted.intended_audience: general American newspaper readership interested in national politics, labor and postwar policy
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-topic newspaper page compiling news briefs and longer items about postwar policy, party platforms, government administration statements, and wartime-to-peacetime transition issues. Primarily reports official statements, legislative proposals and administrative positions for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on organizational political spending
rubrics_metrics.description: "No organization of capital or labor should be permitted, directly or indirectly, to use its funds for any political party or candidate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as part of the Republican declaration; the clause was struck out of a draft by subcommittee action (top-heavy vote) because many Republican representatives had received union support. Shows both recommended standard and political controversy over enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid secrecy, inefficiency and protect American way of life
rubrics_metrics.description: "to avoid secrecy, inefficiency and ... economy in government, and the protection of the American way of life against either Fascist or Communist trends."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an aim/purpose in the Republicans' statement — frames domestic policy as opposing both regimentation and extremist threats; quoted in the program as a guiding principle for policy choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support effective international peace organization (non‑specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Wholehearted support for an effective organization for international peace, without mentioning the United Nations Organization."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement expresses backing for international peace machinery but indicates sensitivity about explicit naming of the UN in some drafts; demonstrates diplomatic/party positioning on multilateral institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for United Nations Organization for international peace
rubrics_metrics.description: "We support the United Nations Organization for international peace."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Another passage (overlapping reporting) directly affirms support for the UN as the forum where the organized conscience of mankind can act; shows party endorsement of multilateral diplomacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of collective bargaining and sanctity of contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: "Approval of the general principle of collective bargaining between management and labor and emphasis on the sanctity of contracts once they are entered into by unions and employers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Republican platform language: supports collective bargaining while stressing that agreements (contracts) must be binding and respected by both sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal aid limited, state/local initiative and avoid socialization
rubrics_metrics.description: "Continued Federal aid for assistance to needy persons unable to care for themselves... must be based on state and local initiative, operation and responsibility, without Federal bureaucratic interference. It must avoid any socialization of the medical profession or of any other activity. Federal aid must be in amounts which do not impose an unreasonable burden of taxation on the rest of the population who pay the bills."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy principle balancing federal support for needy persons with deference to state/local responsibility and explicit opposition to socialization; sets fiscal restraint as a constraint on federal aid levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of adequate national defense
rubrics_metrics.description: "Maintenance of an 'adequate' national defense supported by large reserve forces and a broad program of scientific research."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as part of national defense posture; elsewhere expanded to require a well-trained/equipped Army, Navy and Air Force supported by research, industrial base and reserves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to regimentation and call for strict economy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Criticized 'regimentation' and excessive spending and called for strict economy in Government operation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A domestic-policy criterion: reject permanent wartime-style controls and excessive government expansion; prioritizes fiscal restraint in peacetime governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support inter-American system as regional component
rubrics_metrics.description: "We support the indispensable inter-American system as a regional part of the international organization."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign-policy standard: endorse hemispheric cooperation as part of global peace architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in international relief for humanitarian and stability reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: "We will engage in essential international relief as a humanitarian obligation and to prevent chaos through misery."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions foreign aid both as moral duty and as pragmatic stability policy to avoid postwar disorder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong, solvent, free America as basis for contribution to world peace
rubrics_metrics.description: "We consider that the maintenance of a strong, solvent, free America is the basis of our contribution to world peace."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links domestic economic/financial health and political freedoms to the country's ability to contribute internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense forces readiness and support infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: "We stand for a well trained and fully equipped Army, Navy and Air Force adequate to meet any emergency under future conditions of warfare. It must be supported by the most modern scientific research, a strong industrial system and reserves of trained men with weapons and equipment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed standard for military preparedness emphasizing training, equipment, research, industrial capacity and reserves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of government in promoting prosperity (limited intervention)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Government alone cannot feed the people, nor employ them, nor make the profits from which new enterprises and new jobs are born. Government can help its people to prosperity by lightening the burdens of debt and taxes, laying down the rules of life play and protecting those whose own strength and resources are not sufficient to protect themselves."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulates a limited-government economic role: facilitation, tax/debt relief, and safety nets rather than direct production or profit-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of opportunity for all
rubrics_metrics.description: "We believe that equality of opportunity should be available to all, regardless of race, creed or beginnings. Every individual should be afforded an opportunity to prosper according to his talents, his abilities and his diligence subject only to a like right for his neighbor."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms nondiscrimination and merit-based opportunity as a guiding domestic principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax policy: equitable, stimulative, and simplified
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our tax burden must be equitably distributed. Taxes must be, so as to stimulate creative enterprise, not destroy it, and to afford the individual adequate purchasing power. Tax forms and tax paying must be simplified. There must be an incentive for business to expand production and employment and must be return to both labor and investors..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for tax policy that balances equity with incentives for production and employment, simpler administration, and returns to labor and investors to sustain demand and growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government solvency and balanced outlays
rubrics_metrics.description: "The solvency of our government must be assured. Outlay must be brought in line with income. The value of the dollar must be maintained."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiscal stability criterion: balance budgets (or align outlays with income) and protect currency value as central economic objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return wartime liberties when possible; remove controls
rubrics_metrics.description: "War-time limitations, restrictions and controls must be removed. The instant a right or liberty can be returned to the people, it shall be returned. Neither the war nor any other excuse shall be justification for fastening regimentation permanently upon the American people."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil-liberty standard: roll back controls promptly in peacetime and avoid permanent regimentation under wartime pretexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of labor to organize and protections for collective bargaining
rubrics_metrics.description: "We reaffirm our belief in the right of labor to organize and bargain collectively with employers as one of the cornerstones of competitive enterprise... The processes of such gaining must be protected and strengthened if we are to have real jobs and prosperity for all."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports union rights while emphasizing protection and strengthening of processes (bargaining) rather than substitution by government decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free bargaining and binding contracts; limits on industrial conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: "For that purpose we believe that governmental decision must not be substituted for free agreement, but governmental machinery to promote peaceful settlement of disputes should be improved. Demands by either side must be kept within the bounds of reason and fairness... The desired end of bargaining between management and men is a contract. Once that contract is made, it should and must be equally binding on both parties... free collective bargaining and contracts resulting therefrom must not be nullified or destroyed by resort on either side to willful violence or unlawful destruction of property."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets standards for industrial relations: prefer voluntary agreements, improve dispute-settlement machinery, require reasonableness, and prohibit violent or unlawful tactics that undermine agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal aid to states must avoid unreasonable tax burden
rubrics_metrics.description: "We favor Federal aid to the extent necessary to states, and through states to their sub-divisions to assist them affording subsistence... Federal aid must be in amounts which do not impose an unreasonable burden of taxation on the rest of the population who pay the bills."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiscal constraint on federal transfers: provide necessary aid but limit amounts to avoid unfair burden on taxpayers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for farmers: price stability and rural improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have pledged stability of farm prices during the reconversion and readjustment periods. We will carry out those pledges. We will support sound, permanent proposals to give farmers expanding markets and their fair share of the national income. We reaffirm our long-standing support of soil and water conservation. We shall support measures designed to better rural living."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agricultural policy criteria: stabilize prices during transition, expand markets, ensure fair income share, and support conservation and rural living improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterans' benefits and local responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "A grateful nation demands that those who fought in its defense, their widows and orphans, must never be forgotten. The best of medical care and rehabilitation, education and training for all desiring it and efficient assistance in securing homes, farms, businesses and real jobs, must be provided for the Veteran. Nothing in the Federal program should lessen the responsibility of each local community to provide for the return to civilian life of its gallant sons and daughters in a spirit of understanding, helpfulness and dignity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard for veteran reintegration: comprehensive benefits (medical, rehab, education, training, job/home assistance) with emphasis on local community responsibility and dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Builder pricing limits under Patman bill (housing controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Patman bill language reported: a builder would be allowed 'a legal price' on his materials and services, plus current labor costs, plus the same margin of profit that was made on comparable construction in 1941; any builder caught making an 'excessive profit, over and above that enjoyed by the industry in 1941,' would be liable to a suit for damages (three times the amount was mentioned elsewhere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/legislative pricing standard for low-cost housing construction to limit postwar profiteering; enforcement via damages and legal remedies; intended to keep homes 'reasonably priced' for veterans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for up-to-date parity formula for farm price support
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinton P. Anderson called for an 'up-to-date' Government parity formula, criticizing the present formula as a 'patchwork of special provisions' that yields too-high prices for some commodities and too-low for others and which impedes sound agricultural planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative standard: parity formula used to set support prices must be modernized and consistent across commodities to enable effective agricultural planning and consumption stabilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for restoring privileges on frozen foreign assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Treasury announced that the U.S. will relinquish control of new assets/transactions with most nations but will retain controls for countries that have not taken effective measures to control/dispose of enemy assets (e.g., Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Tangier, Germany and Japan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural standard: privileges to transact and unfreeze assets are conditional on foreign governments taking effective steps to immobilize and account for enemy holdings and reach satisfactory arrangements on disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on import of securities and currency
rubrics_metrics.description: Under existing Treasury regulation, securities and currency still may not be imported into the United States from the majority of foreign nations, regardless of licensing or unblocking conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory rule retained in peacetime transition to control financial flows and manage economic/security risks from foreign sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific property protection and responsible disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Karl T. Compton protested the Army's destruction of Japanese cyclotrons as 'an act of utter stupidity' and argued that cyclotrons are not instruments capable of producing atomic bombs and that regulations should safeguard scientific work rather than destroying valuable equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy standard: protect scientific infrastructure and use reasonable regulations to safeguard sensitive research while preserving capacity for peaceful scientific work; calls for review/housecleaning where military orders damaged scientific resources unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: International inspection/access to prevent atomic-arms race (policy position)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rep. Joseph E. Talbot warned that retaining atomic secrets would provoke a frantic arms race and suggested that a world organization prohibiting atomic force would need access to 'every laboratory and every industrial plant in every nation of the world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy criterion advocating transparency and universal inspection powers for any international regime seeking to prohibit atomic weapons to prevent clandestine proliferation and arms races.
